handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

key_findings_and_decisions: PROPOSAL PARSING (validated against signed PDFs): the RENDERED value of a Word field is cost truth; the raw `=N` formula can be stale in EITHER direction (line items AND grand totals). Parser stores both and flags mismatches. Also handled: OPTIONAL items listed BELOW 'Grand Total:' are excluded from it; quantity cells that are bare numbers with no field code (Mountainside); grand totals that are bare '$...' text several blank lines below the label (Killdeer). Header client/address is inconsistently FORMTEXT-marked, so IDENTITY COMES FROM THE MANIFEST, not the proposal header.

CANONICAL JOB TOTAL = total_reconciled (sum of line items). grand_total (the as-quoted / signed-PDF bid) is preserved alongside, plus total_unreconciled_delta. 7 of 8 jobs foot to the penny ($0.00). Only Settlement Mountain diverges: reconciled 2,123,245.75 vs quoted 2,267,145.75, delta +143,900 (an unitemized markup in Brian's doc) -> flagged total_unreconciled. Rule documented in schema §4.3.

DWG EXTRACTION IS UNRELIABLE FOR COUNTS/CURB but this is NOT a Phase-1 blocker. Diagnosis on Painted Rock (generated qty sheet vs ground truth data/25068-2/qty_tbl_25068.txt): clean pipe lengths ~1% (sewer 806 vs 802, water 837 vs 830) and road alignment good; BUT 4 defects -> (1) anonymous dynamic-block explosion: 94 phantom *U### inserts (42 storm / 28 water / 22 sewer) vs truth 5 drywells / 4 manholes / 5 valves; (2) curb exactly 3.0x over (SF-CURB-PROP-LIN 7,109 LF vs truth 2,360 — multiple parallel curb lines on one layer); (3) multi-file double-count (BASE+DESIGN+TOPO merged); (4) ROW width / lot count / stripping depth / scuppers genuinely not in basemap geometry. REFRAME: the proposal already carries the as-bid quantity AND price for every line item, so for Phase 1 the trustworthy spine is PROPOSALS + QTY SHEETS; DWG is tertiary (good only for pipe LF + road-alignment LF as scale metrics / cross-check). DWG deep fixes (resolve dynamic-block names, curb-line dedup, design-file-only) are DEFERRED/PARKED at Nolan's direction.

normalize_dwg currently still PROMOTES the bad curb (7,109) and inflated named manhole/drywell counts. Acceptable for now because DWG quantities are clearly source-tagged and kept separate from the proposal; do NOT trust those specific DWG fields until the DWG extraction is fixed.

QTY SHEET PARSING added to M1. qty_tbl_*.txt is a uniform clean markdown table (group | work type | unit | TAKEOFF | QTY | notes). Parsed for all 8: ROW_SF extracted for all (Woodman 81,757 / Painted Rock 84,558 match ground truth), stripping depth for 7/8 (Mountainside has none stated; Expo label says 2" but its own note says 18" — inconsistency preserved in the row's notes for manual review). The .xlsx is left UNPARSED by design — the .txt is quantities-only (has_pricing=false), which answers PRD open question 17.4.

VERSION ALIGNMENT is a MANUAL gate (Nolan's call): per job the plan PDF, DWG, qty sheet, and proposal may be different design revisions (several plan PDFs are explicitly PRELIM/Preliminary). NOT automated (file mtimes are unreliable copy-dates; filename dates partial). Recorded in PRD §16 + memory + README.

DWGs are now LOCALLY AVAILABLE FOR ALL 8 JOBS (Nolan added them this session) in varied layouts: job-folder root (Settlement/Killdeer/Expo/Lone Fir/Solara), nested 'CAD FILES/...' (Mountainside), test_copies/ (Woodman/Painted Rock). py1 derives its TESTS output folder name from basename(dwg_dir) = dwg_test_name. XREFs (VBASE) count as a single insert in py1, so processing them as separate --files is additive, not double-counting.

prior_sessions_summary.2026_6_2.4_phase1_kickoff: Conversation-first requirements identification for Phase 1. Wrote the PRD (phase1/PRD_phase1_quick_job_budget_generation.md). Established: TWO-SYSTEM architecture (A = offline knowledge building from DWG+proposal+qty/plans into a case library + knowledge pack; B = runtime single-sheet inference by analogy + pattern gap-fill). 'Learning' = persist knowledge as data + retrieve into context (RAG/in-context), NO model training. Output = line-item + total + confidence band + provenance; target 10-15% of historical total. RAG deferred (load all cases in context until ~50 jobs). Confirmed proposals are parseable .doc form exports. Job NAME is the stable key (folder numbers are proposal numbers). Foundry excluded.
prior_sessions_summary.phase0_arc: Phase 0 = plan files -> HeavyBid quantity sheet (quantities only). Built a blind firm-agnostic DWG extractor (phase0_new/py1) + Claude qty-sheet generator (py4); validated on Woodman (block counts exact, pipe lengths ~3%). Plan PDFs are fully rasterized so DWG is the geometry path. Typical-section facts (ROW width, stripping depth, paving) are the historically hardest to extract from geometry. Full detail: _handoffs/phase0_qty_sheet_generation/2026_6_2.FINAL_summary_handoff.json.
prior_sessions_summary.phase0_to_phase1_bridge_finding_this_ses: Phase 0's premise that DWG extraction is 'the trustworthy spine' does NOT carry to Phase 1: because past jobs already have finished proposals (as-bid quantities + prices), Phase 1's spine is proposals + qty sheets, and the DWG's role shrinks to scale metrics + cross-check. This is why DWG extraction defects, while real, do not block M1.
